transcript:
Header: 2026-12-15 16:00 PST | Duration: ~52m | Recording: cloud | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood Solutions), Elena (StratusPay Head of ML), Tom (VP Eng), Sofia (SRE), Rahul (PM)

[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call and then we'll jump into the POC timeline and the benchmark plan.
[00:12] Elena Ruiz: Hi yep Elena here.
[00:14] Tom Becker: Tom, thanks.
[00:16] Sofia Kim: Sofia.
[00:17] Rahul Desai: Rahul.
[00:19] Maya Patel: Maya here from Redwood.
[00:22] Liam O'Connor: Liam, waving.
[00:25] Jordan Kim: Great. Agenda is: confirm success criteria, what access we need, sizing and benchmark plan, and then pin the midpoint and exec readout dates.
[00:34] Elena Ruiz: Sounds good. We're especially interested in latency at peak and cost per 1M tokens — want to see if this is economical for real-time fraud scoring.
[00:44] Tom Becker: To add, our engineering leads want to see a throughput test that reflects bursty traffic — roughly 800 qps sustained for 30s, with peaks to 2k qps for a few seconds.
[00:56] Maya Patel: Okay that's useful. Just so we're clear, are those numbers production or a scoped slice for the POC?
[01:02] Tom Becker: That's representative, but we'll provide exact slices. For the POC we're okay with a scaled-down replica if you need it, but we'd like projection guidance.
[01:12] Jordan Kim: For timeline expectations, we usually run a three milestone POC: kickoff/access, midpoint perf validation, and exec readout. We'll map gates per milestone. Does that fit your timelines?
[01:21] Rahul Desai: Yes, but exec readout needs to align with our Q1 budget review — week of Jan 10-15 ideally.
[01:28] Jordan Kim: Noted — we can aim midpoint review ~Jan 5, exec readout Jan 12.
[01:34] Elena Ruiz: That gives us time to vet security too. On that note, what exact access do you need? VPC peering, KMS test key, maybe a read-only S3 bucket?
[01:44] Maya Patel: We typically need a temporary test VPC peering or customer-provided bastion, sample KMS key for encrypt/decrypt in a test namespace, and a sample dataset blob in S3 for token distribution. Also, audit log access to validate end-to-end.
[01:58] Sofia Kim: We need to confirm our security team will allow KMS creds in the sandbox. We can create a scoped key with rotation.
[02:06] Tom Becker: Any compliance artifacts you need from us?
[02:09] Liam O'Connor: We'll share our SOC 2 Type II whitepaper and the standard security checklist; but for initial perf tests we only need scoped dev credentials. We'll still sign an NDA/SSLA if needed.
[02:20] Rahul Desai: Good. On success criteria, we want: p95 latency under 120ms for the scoring model at 800 qps scaled test, error rate <0.1%, and per-1M token cost under $XX — open to Redwood suggesting the cost target.
[02:35] Maya Patel: We'll put proposed cost bands in the benchmark workbook. For pass/fail we can define soft and hard thresholds. Soft: p95 <150ms; hard: p95 <200ms; error rate hard threshold 0.5%.
[02:48] Elena Ruiz: The fraud model average token length is small — 18 tokens for prompt, 12 tokens output, so tokenization is compact. We'll put a sample payload.
[02:58] Jordan Kim: Great, helps kernel selection. On tooling, we usually run two kinds of tests: synthetic load (k6/jmeter) to validate throughput and a production-replay test to check real token distributions. We'll provide a tiny harness to replay logs — need a sample log export from you.
[03:12] Tom Becker: We'll export a 24-hour slice that mirrors burst patterns.
[03:16] Maya Patel: Perfect. Regarding benchmarks, we'll measure latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), throughput, token cost, and cold-start vs warm-cache behavior. Also KV cache hit rates if you test session-based flows.
[03:30] Elena Ruiz: We do use KV cache heavily for user history, so please include a run with cache warm and another with cache cold.
[03:37] Jordan Kim: Noted. Now let's break down the milestone deliverables and who owns what.
[03:42] [03:42] Jordan Kim: Milestone 1 (Kickoff & Access) — deliverables: VPC/KMS access, sample dataset, initial sizing doc from customer, Redwood security docs. Target completion: 2026-12-18.
[03:57] Elena Ruiz: Can you list exact ports and peering details?
[04:01] Maya Patel: We'll send a checklist with IP ranges, peering steps, and example IAM roles. I'll email that after the call.
[04:07] Jordan Kim: Milestone 2 (Midpoint Perf Review) — Redwood runs baseline benchmarks and shares a perf snapshot and cost projection. Proposed date: 2027-01-05.
[04:18] Tom Becker: Who from our side should be on that review? Likely Elena, me, and our infra lead.
[04:22] Jordan Kim: Works. Milestone 3 (Exec Readout) — a 30-minute exec level presentation with results, recommended dev plan, and commercialization options. Target: 2027-01-12.
[04:35] Rahul Desai: Expect to invite CFO and Head of Ops to that readout.
[04:39] Maya Patel: We'll prepare two slides for cost scenarios: conservative and aggressive.
[04:44] Elena Ruiz: About failure modes — what happens if we don't meet p95? Is there a fallback to a cheaper but slower model variant?
[04:51] Liam O'Connor: Yes, smart routing can fall back to a compatible model variant; we can set routing policies for latency vs cost. We'll show an A/B of variants in the benchmark.
[05:00] Tom Becker: Also curious about quantization options and how that affects repro and accuracy.
[05:04] Maya Patel: We'll surface expected quality regression metrics in the workbook and include a small eval suite so you can see any drop in scoring fidelity.
[05:13] Elena Ruiz: Sounds good. Can you also share how cost per token is computed? We have some internal ways they count tokens and need matching.
[05:20] Jordan Kim: We'll document the cost model: tokens in + tokens out, batching efficiency, KV cache savings. We'll include sample calculations in the workbook.
[05:29] Rahul Desai: About timelines — if access takes longer, does the midpoint shift?
[05:33] Jordan Kim: It'll be flexible, but we need the kickoff access gate by Dec 18 to hit the Jan 5 midpoint. If access slips, we'll re-baseline and notify stakeholders.
[05:42] Elena Ruiz: Our security review is on Dec 16, hope to approve. If they push back, we'll escalate.
[05:47] Maya Patel: We can run a limited host-side benchmark without full VPC if needed, but it won't reflect production egress and peering latencies. We'll mark that as a risk.
[05:57] Jordan Kim: Risk log: 1) Access delays, 2) Unexpected token distribution differences, 3) KMS permissions complexity. We'll track and mitigate.
[06:06] Tom Becker: For reporting cadence, weekly syncs are fine — short 30m standups.
[06:10] Elena Ruiz: Agree.
[06:12] Maya Patel: I'll set up a shared drive and the benchmark workbook link after this call. Deck link: https://redwood.ai/poc/deck-stratuspay (placeholder). Benchmark workbook: https://redwood.ai/poc/bb-stratuspay (will be shared).
[06:25] Jordan Kim: Quick recap and next steps: Maya to share checklist and workbook by 12/18, Elena to provide VPC/KMS creds by 12/17, Jordan to send pilot pricing by 12/19, Tom to give exact traffic slices by 12/16. Midpoint perf review 2027-01-05, exec readout 2027-01-12.
[06:45] Elena Ruiz: That covers it, thanks.
[06:47] Rahul Desai: Thanks team.
[06:49] Jordan Kim: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email and create the weekly cadence calendar invite. Meeting end.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts present (e.g., "RTE" transcribed as "artie" in one section), speaker names occasionally generic in export. Links are placeholders and will be updated.
